title: Third-Party Vendor Coordination and Escalation Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the customer-success and engineering operational procedures for incidents where a third-party vendor (cloud provider, telemetry backend, datastore, or network provider) materially impacts enterprise customer availability, latency, or data integrity. It focuses on coordination, authoritative communication, and minimizing customer impact while preserving evidence and contractual obligations.

Scope and when to use this playbook:
- Applies to enterprise customers (Dedicated & Private).
- Trigger conditions (use if ANY apply):
  1) Customer reports degraded responses traceable to external dependency (timeouts, 5xxs with vendor path).
  2) Platform telemetry shows cross-tenant error spikes correlated to external service call failures.
  3) Vendor posts a public incident with potential impact to Redwood-hosted tenants.
- Not for: routine internal service outages fully owned and resolved by Redwood (use standard incident runbooks).

Stakeholders and roles:
- Customer Success Lead (CSL) — primary point for customer communication and SLA negotiation.
- Incident Commander (IC) — typically eng-sre on-call; owns technical coordination and declaration.
- Vendor Liaison (VL) — support/partner engineering contact who interfaces with vendor support and legal (if needed).
- Product Owner (PO) — evaluates feature or model impact and approves workaround rollouts.
- Legal & Compliance — engaged if data exposure or contractual breaches suspected.
- Solutions Engineer (SE) — assists with customer-specific configuration changes and rollback.

Escalation matrix (decision table):
| Symptom | First responder | Escalate to | External contact window | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Transient API 429/5xx from vendor | On-call SRE | VL within 15m | Contact vendor support (priority P2) | Add correlation IDs to ticket |
| Sustained degraded throughput >20% 30m | IC + CSL | Product & Legal | Vendor account manager within 30m | Consider traffic-shaping fallback |
| Data loss or divergence | IC + Legal | CTO + Vendor Exec | Escalate to vendor SE/Legal immediately (30m) | Preserve logs, avoid write operations |

Immediate steps (first 30 minutes):
1) Triage and classify:
   - Confirm customer-facing scope (single tenant, cohort, global).
   - Collect identifiers: tenant_id, request_ids, sample timestamps (UTC), error codes.
2) Contain impact:
   - If possible, enable safe-fail: route affected customers to compatible model-variant or degraded mode.
   - Apply rate-limits at gateway for noisy tenants.
3) Open authoritative incident:
   - Create incident in PagerDuty with severity: P2 (degraded) or P1 (outage).
   - Populate incident ticket with vendor name, ticket ID (if already opened), sample traces, and correlation query links.
4) Vendor engagement:
   - VL opens ticket with vendor, attaching RBAC-limited logs and correlation IDs. Use the following template (replace bracketed fields):

   Subject: "Redwood Incident [INC-<id>] — [Vendor] API timeouts impacting enterprise tenants"

   Body:
   - Redwood Incident ID: [INC-<id>]
   - Time window (UTC): [start..end]
   - Affected tenant(s): [tenant-ids]
   - Observable symptoms: [5xx rate, latency, failed writes]
   - Correlation IDs / traces: [links]
   - Priority: P2 (Customer-impacting).

   Attach: sanitized logs, network traceroutes, and sample payloads.

Customer communications (templates and cadence):
- Initial acknowledgement (within 30m): short, factual, owner, next update ETA.
  "Hello <CustomerName>, we are aware of an issue affecting <feature>. Our on-call team has identified this is related to <vendor>. We are investigating and will update within 60 minutes. Owner: <CSL-name> (email/phone)."
- Status update (every 60m while active): include scope, mitigation steps, ETA, and whether workaround is available.
- Post-incident summary (within 48h): include root cause (if known), impact, mitigations, and corrective actions.

Vendor coordination checklist (practical items):
- Authorization and access:
  - Verify support contract & escalation path (AM, Technical Account Manager (TAM), SE).
  - Confirm least-privilege data exchange: generate temporary log bundles, masked PII.
- Evidence collection:
  - Time-synced traces (UTC), service mesh spans, TCP dumps (pcap), and error-rate time series.
  - Preserve raw artifacts for 14 days in secure bucket: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/<INC-id>/ (do not modify).
- Workaround validation:
  - Test traffic shaping / fallback in staging tenant before applying to production.
  - Document rollback steps for each change.
- SLA & credit assessment:
  - VL and Legal to map incident to vendor SLOs and customer contract terms within 72 hours.

Telemetry queries and diagnostics (examples):
- Prometheus: error-rate by target_vendor
  query: rate(http_requests_total{vendor="X",code=~"5.."}[5m])
- Traces: sample span filter (Jaeger/Zipkin)
  filter: span.tags.vendor == "X" && span.tags.http.status_code >= 500
- SQL: find impacted tenant list (example)
  SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as failures FROM request_log WHERE vendor = 'X' AND timestamp >= '2026-02-12T00:00:00Z' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY failures DESC LIMIT 50;
- Network: tcpdump capture guidance
  sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host <vendor-ip> and port <vendor-port> -w /tmp/vendor-<INC-id>.pcap

Communication ownership matrix:
- Initial customer acknowledgement: CSL (within 30m)
- Technical updates: IC/VL (every 60m)
- Executive escalation & legal notices: VP Customer Success / Legal (as required)
- Final root-cause & QBR summary: CSL + PO (deliver within 48h; include mitigation plan for next 90 days)

Templated escalation email to vendor (short form):
"Hello <VendorSupport>,

We are Redwood Inc (Account: <account-id>). We are experiencing increased 5xx rates when calling <api-endpoint>. Incident ID: <INC-id>. Please escalate internally to engineering and share ETA. We can provide traces and pcap. Contact: <VL-email> + <VL-phone>.

Regards,
Vendor Liaison — Redwood"

Rollback and change control guidance:
- Every workaround that modifies routing, quotas, or model variants requires:
  - a short risk assessment,
  - approval by IC and PO,
  - automated rollback configured and smoke test passing within 10 minutes.
- Changes must be recorded in change-log and synchronized to customer CSL.

Post-incident actions and artifacts (within 72h):
1) Evidence bucket review and retention confirmation.
2) RCA draft: root cause, contributing factors, timeline, and customer impact table (tenant-level).
3) Customer remediation plan: fixes, timeline, and compensatory credit if applicable.
4) Vendor follow-up: request for technical write-up and SLA response.
5) Preventative actions: add probes, synthetic checks, or alternate vendor routing where warranted.
6) QBR item: include incident summary, change plan, and KPIs for next quarter.

- Useful internal links:
  - Incident channel: #inc-redwood-production (Slack)

Appendix B — Frequently asked questions:
Q: When do we issue an SLA credit to customers?
A: Follow customer contract rules; use the customer-impact table from the RCA and coordinate with Legal and Finance for any credits.

Q: Can we switch vendors for an impacted tenant?
A: Short-term fallbacks (cache-only, degraded model variant) are preferred. Vendor switches require Product approval and at least one-week lead time for provisioning.

Appendix C — Quick triage checklist (printable):
1) Create incident & set severity. 2) Notify CSL & affected customers (30m). 3) Collect traces & preserve pcap. 4) Open vendor ticket with correlation IDs. 5) Test and apply fallback if safe. 6) Schedule RCA and customer summary within 48h.

End of document.
